It operates exclusively B2B, selling to institutional buyers (textile manufacturers, garment exporters, bulk purchasers, fabric processors) via direct sales and a broker/agent network domestically, with opportunistic exports …

business_ops.seasonality: Cotton procurement is seasonal: buffer stock of cotton bales is built during the peak procurement season coinciding with India's cotton harvest (October to March), when availability is high and prices relatively low; pledge loan facilities are availed against stocked bales during this period. Export sales are opportunistic, undertaken typically during periods of low domestic demand or to meet export obligations, so export revenues are not consistent year-on-year.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Fully integrated spinning facility covering all stages from cotton bale procurement, cleaning, carding, combing, spinning and winding to final yarn packaging at a single location. Backward linkage: principal raw material (cotton bales) procured through a network of brokers from ginning mills and traders across Gujarat, Maharashtra, Haryana and Madhya Pradesh; 123 / 149 / 147 / 174 suppliers in H1FY26 / FY25 / FY24 / FY23, of which 6 suppliers associated for over four years contributed 45.47%, 70.68% and 42.01% of total purchases in H1FY26, FY25 and FY24-FY23 periods as stated. Five in-house TFO (two-for-one) twisting machines (procured May 2025, scheduled operational from July 2025) described as a significant step toward full vertical integration for value-added yarns (Eli Twist, Lycra-blended). Captive renewable power: 1.2 MW rooftop solar operational July 2024, 6.1 MW ground-mounted solar (5 MW commissioned) and a proposed 4.2 MW wind project. Forward linkage: exclusively B2B sales - domestic via direct sales to institutional customers plus a network of 8 third-party brokers and agents (as of September 30, 2025); all exports routed through merchant exporters. Named long-standing institutional customers include Welspun Living Limited and Jindal Worldwide Limited. Working capital: sanctioned pledge loan limit of Rs 2,000 lakhs from Axis Bank Limited against cotton bale inventory.

overview.business_model: Manufactures and sells cotton yarn from its Manufacturing Facility at Gondal, Rajkot (Gujarat), which was expanded by adding 6 spinning machines to the existing 11 compact ring spinning machines, raising capacity from 5,500.00 MT/annum to 9,855.00 MT/annum. Sales are made on a purchase-order basis without long-term customer contracts; revenue is highly concentrated — top-1 customer contributed 28.57% (six months ended September 30, 2025), 32.97% (Fiscal 2025), 44.35% (Fiscal 2024) and 37.26% (Fiscal 2023) of revenue, top-10 customers 79.74%-86.36% — and geographically concentrated in Gujarat (87.72% of revenue in H1 FY26, 93.48% in Fiscal 2025, 83.14% in Fiscal 2024, 85.59% in Fiscal 2023). Revenue from operations was Rs 25,504.4 lakh in Fiscal 2025 and Rs 13,208 lakh in the six-month period ended September 30, 2025 (per the customer-concentration table).

internal_operational.detail: Revenue heavily dependent on a limited number of customers; business conducted on purchase-order basis without long-term contracts, exposing the company to customer attrition and production-planning challenges. No key customer loss in H1 FY26 or last three fiscals, but no assurance for the future.
internal_operational.title: Customer concentration with no long-term contracts

internal_operational.detail: Manufacturing Facility and Registered Office located in Gondal, Rajkot, Gujarat, and Gujarat contributes a major share of revenue; any regional disruption (regulation, labour unrest, natural calamity, unrest, health emergency) would have a disproportionate effect. Only disruption to date was temporary COVID-19 restrictions.
internal_operational.title: Geographic concentration in Gujarat

internal_operational.detail: Cotton bales are the principal raw material (more than half of production cost), sourced via brokers/agents from ginning mills; no long-term supply agreements (spot/short-term purchases); cotton prices highly volatile (yield, climate, MSP, government policy, geopolitics, e.g. Bangladesh unrest); buffer stock procured October-March is pledged to lenders; overstocking/understocking risks.
internal_operational.evidence: Raw material purchases: ₹9,634.02 lakh (72.94% of revenue, H1 FY26), ₹16,890.47 lakh (66.23%, FY25), ₹17,631.29 lakh (76.13%, FY24), ₹15,571.01 lakh (73.07%, FY23); Top 1 supplier: 27.37%/32.11%/22.07%/16.84% of purchases; Top 5: 81.72%/73.31%/61.71%/47.58%; Top 10: 93.98%/85.15%/81.82%/63.28%; sanctioned pledge limit ₹2,000 lakh from Axis Bank against cotton inventory
internal_operational.title: Supplier concentration and cotton supply/price risk

strategy_growth.detail: Planned captive wind plant (EPC by Suzlon Energy Limited, funded entirely from Net Proceeds) has no definitive EPC contract or binding agreement as on date; delay/failure defers expected December 2026 commencement, cost savings, and energy-banking synergy with solar under GERC Green Energy Open Access Regulations 2024; IPO under-subscription or reallocation would further affect the project.
strategy_growth.evidence: 4.2 MW wind project; expected commencement December 2026; grid electricity accounts for 6%-7% of cost structure; banking limit 30% of monthly consumption under GERC policy
strategy_growth.title: No definitive agreement yet for proposed 4.2 MW wind power project

strategy_growth.detail: Fragmented Indian spinning industry; competitors with longer histories, greater scale, cheaper inputs and capital can pressure pricing and credit terms; consumer shift from cotton to synthetic yarns (polyester, nylon, elastane - cheaper, durable, fast-fashion suited) threatens demand; failure to adapt may cost market share and utilization.
strategy_growth.evidence: Competition from large integrated domestic mills, vertically integrated groups and international low-cost suppliers
strategy_growth.title: Competitive industry and shift towards synthetic textiles

strategy_growth.detail: Project in planning phase; purchase order for two Suzlon WTGs (Model S120_140) not yet placed; timely execution depends on land acquisition, approvals (GEDA, GETCO, SLDC), grid connectivity and Suzlon performance (EPC plus 5-year O&M); funding shortfall or cost escalation would require internal accruals/debt; generation depends on wind availability; turbines face obsolescence over 25-year lifespan.
strategy_growth.evidence: Capex ₹3,900 lakh funded entirely from Net Proceeds; expected output approximately 136-140 lakh units annually; cost escalation triggers cited: exchange rate above ₹82/USD, steel prices above ₹58,000/MT; commissioning expected December 2026
strategy_growth.title: Execution, funding, regulatory, operational and technology risks of the 4.2 MW wind project

concerns_observed: Severe customer concentration: top-1 customer contributed 28.57%-44.35% of revenue and top-10 contributed 79.74%-86.36%, all on purchase-order basis with no long-term contracts.
Geographic concentration in Gujarat (83.14%-93.48% of revenue) from a single manufacturing facility, so any regional disruption is disproportionate.
Supplier concentration rising sharply: top-5 suppliers moved from 47.59% (FY23) to 81.72% of purchases (H1 FY26), against volatile, spot-purchased cotton that is over half of production cost.

Cash flow quality is uneven: CFO was negative Rs 491 lakh in FY24 (driven by a Rs 2,369 lakh receivables build) while PAT was positive Rs 655 lakh; large inventory builds recur (Rs 3,998 lakh FY25, Rs 2,350 lakh H1 FY26).

Governance and compliance flags: promoter Bhaveshbhai Ramani appears on the RoC struck-off-company directors list (Ecore Spinning); auditor churn within a year (Finava resigned Jan 2025, replaced by Doshi Doshi & Co); company secretary appointed only March 2024 despite the Section 203 threshold being crossed in FY2017; 10 delayed MCA filings with suo-moto adjudication pending.

Pre-Issue promoter holding is only 47.07% and the register has just 22 shareholders, every one holding 1% or more; large intra-family nil-cost gift transfers occurred in November 2023 and a 1.5:1 bonus in March 2024.

Rs 3,900 lakh (of Rs 6,123.55 lakh capex) 4.2 MW wind project is unfunded except from Net Proceeds, has no binding EPC contract and no purchase order placed, with commissioning only expected by December 2026; deployment is not appraised by any bank or independent agency.
